name: NPR Tiny Desk Concerts
description: Intimate musical performances, recorded live at the desk of All Songs Considered host Bob Boilen.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Family Hour: Gaelynn Lea
videos.overview: The former Tiny Desk Contest winner brought the crowd to its collective feet.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Family Hour: Cautious Clay
videos.overview: The Brooklyn-based artist, in addition to offering up an impeccable vocal performance, brought perhaps the only flute solo of SXSW 2019 to NPR Music's Tiny Desk Family Hour.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Family Hour: John Paul White
videos.overview: The former Civil Wars star performed a new song that even makes his kids cry.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Family Hour: Mountain Man
videos.overview: We couldn't pick just one song from the trio's appearance at the Tiny Desk Family hour. So we went with three.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Family Hour: Wyclef Jean
videos.overview: The former Fugees star brought an electric guitar and a young protégé.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Family Hour: Gina Chavez
videos.overview: In this performance of "The Sweet Sound Of Your Name," a song of devotion from 2014, the Austin singer-songwriter finds magic in the intimacy of a communal setting.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Family Hour: Fragile Rock
videos.overview: Fragile Rock's rowdy emo songs are performed by bickering puppets. Onstage at a church in Austin, the band savages the patriarchy in "Smile More."

videos.title: Tiny Desk Family Hour: Amanda Palmer
videos.overview: The intense singer-songwriter performed "The Ride" on a grand piano.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Family Hour: Leikeli47
videos.overview: The charismatic, genre-smashing masked rapper closes NPR Music's big night with intensity, joy and free-wheeling fervor.

videos.title: Ty Dolla $ign Pays Tribute To Mac Miller At The Tiny Desk
videos.overview: While Ty Dolla $ign visited NPR to record his own Tiny Desk concert, he also performed a special tribute to his friend, the late Mac Miller.

videos.title: Megan Thee Stallion
videos.overview: The secret's out! One of 2019's brightest new stars peformed a live show at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Sheryl Crow
videos.overview: Tuesday night's guest star just wants to have some fun behind the Tiny Desk. She'll revisit her classics and perform new songs from her album Threads.

videos.title: Wale
videos.overview: The chart-topping Washington, D.C., rapper brings his songs to life at the Tiny Desk with the help of a six-piece go-go band.

videos.title: Raphael Saadiq
videos.overview: What a way to wrap up Tiny Desk Fest. Raphael Saadiq, one of the most respected voices in soul music, performs a live concert with rising R&B star Lucky Daye.

videos.title: Harry Styles Explains His Love Of The Packers
videos.overview: The English pop star has a Packers logo tattooed on his upper arm. So NPR Music's biggest Packers fan sat him down at the Tiny Desk to ask: What's the deal with that?

videos.title: Tiny Desk Meets globalFEST: Dedicated Men Of Zion, Labess, Sofia Rei & DakhaBrakha
videos.overview: Our first night of live performances features music from Algeria, Argentina, Ukraine and North Carolina.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Meets globalFEST: Minyo Crusaders, Hit La Rosa, Natu Camara, Emel
videos.overview: The second night of our virtual festival features music from Japan, Peru, Guinea and Tunisia.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Meets globalFEST: Vox Sambou, Aditya Prakash, Martha Redbone And More
videos.overview: Wednesday night's showcases blends the sounds of Haiti, India, Italy and the Indigenous people of North America.

videos.title: Tiny Desk Meets globalFEST: Edwin Perez, Elisapie, Nora Brown, Rokia Traoré
videos.overview: Our final night of globalFEST 2021 features salsa, First Nations music, Appalachian folk and a West African superstar.

videos.title: Laura Gibson
videos.overview: Laura Gibson works through a handful of tenderhearted songs: two of them unreleased and two of them from her full-length debut, If You Come to Greet Me.

videos.title: Vic Chesnutt
videos.overview: When Athens, Ga., songwriter Vic Chesnutt was on tour in support of his album, “North Star Deserter,” he stopped by NPR to perform live at All Songs Considered host Bob Boilen's desk. Chesnutt played five songs, including two entirely new ones.

videos.title: Sam Phillips
videos.overview: The music of Sam Phillips unfolds like perfect, miniature pop dramas. Of all her incarnations as a performer — first as a Christian singer, then as a pop singer — the current Sam Phillips is one of the most alluring. Phillips performs four songs from “Don't Do Anything.”

videos.title: Sera Cahoone
videos.overview: Sera Cahoone got her start playing drums for a few widely adored bands in the Pacific Northwest, most notably Band of Horses and the spell-checker-defying Carissa's Wierd. But her self-titled, self-released 2006 album marked her as a fully formed talent — a warm and inviting singer whose songs convey world-weariness and homespun grace.

videos.title: Thao Nguyen
videos.overview: Thao Nguyen makes captivating music. Her songs are raw and infectious, her voice has a distinctive swagger, and she's a remarkably nimble guitarist.

videos.title: Lambchop's Kurt Wagner
videos.overview: Kurt Wagner writes and sings beautiful songs with Lambchop, a hefty Nashville ensemble with a calm, restrained sound. When Kurt Wagner came by the office to play a Tiny Desk Concert, he came alone, with just an acoustic guitar, a stack of lyrics and his humble, good-natured sense of humor.

videos.title: Dr. Dog
videos.overview: Dr. Dog isn't an obvious choice for one of NPR Music's Tiny Desk Concerts. For one thing, it's a pretty big group, at least for the small space behind Bob Boilen's desk. The band's music can be pretty chaotic — loud and rumbling, with multiple instruments fighting to be heard. And singer Toby Leaman likes to belt out his vocals in a window-rattling, raspy growl.

videos.title: Jim White
videos.overview: Jim White is a storyteller first and a musician second. It's a kind of storytelling rooted in his own unusual history: He grew up in Florida in a deeply Pentecostal community and fell in love with the white gospel music he heard. But from there, White took a surprising path to becoming a full-time musician. He was a professional surfer, a boxer, a fashion model in Milan and a cab driver in New York City. White's travels recently took him to Washington, D.C., where he stopped by the offices of NPR Music for this live performance.

videos.title: Shearwater
videos.overview: A glorious four-song set that's at once pristine and ramshackle — equal parts clarity and clatter — not to mention one of our best Tiny Desk Concerts yet.

videos.title: Dave Dondero
videos.overview: He should be a name everyone knows by now. Instead, troubadour David Dondero returned to NPR having slept the night before in his car. Dondero travels from club to club, singing his well-crafted songs — songs that have his signature lyrics at their core. His lyrics can make you smile with their wit and hurt with their bite, all at the same time.

videos.overview: In the band's hands, East African music comes alive in a mix of tradition and contemporary sounds.

videos.title: Gucci Mane
videos.overview: The rapper has spent the year on an extended victory tour. Here are the spoils.

videos.title: Derek Gripper
videos.overview: The classically trained guitarist performs songs originally written for the kora.

videos.title: The Oh Hellos
videos.overview: The nine-piece band returns to the Tiny Desk to fill the air with fake snow and real joy.

videos.title: Declan McKenna
videos.overview: Hear the spirited young singer-songwriter take on religion, poverty and politics, armed with just a guitar and some unrelenting hooks.

videos.title: Donny McCaslin
videos.overview: Hear McCaslin, the saxophonist and bandleader whose group backed David Bowie on Blackstar, near the anniversary of that album's release. Selections include an instrumental take on Bowie's "Lazarus."

videos.title: Lila Downs
videos.overview: With a voice that borrows heavily from opera, Downs performs the kind of full-throated mariachi singing that would fit right in at Mexico City's Garibaldi Square — ground zero for mariachi.

videos.title: Brent Cobb
videos.overview: Cobb's words shimmer like a tall glass of sweet tea in the late-morning sun. Watch the country singer-songwriter perform four songs from his debut album.

videos.title: BADBADNOTGOOD
videos.overview: The jazz band, known for its soulful interpretations of songs by Nas and Ol' Dirty Bastard, plays its own new material live in the NPR Music offices.

videos.title: Miramar
videos.overview: Watch the Virginia band sweep the NPR crowd off its feet with a collection of exquisite boleros by Puerto Rican composer Sylvia Rexach.

videos.title: Gallant
videos.overview: The rising R&B star performs three falsetto-drenched highlights from his 2016 debut, Ology — including "Bourbon," which features a guest rap from Chance The Rapper collaborator Saba.

videos.title: D.R.A.M.
videos.overview: The rapper/singer storms the NPR Music offices, activating his signature smile and bouncing through five highlights from his catalog — including the smash single "Broccoli."

videos.title: Run The Jewels
videos.overview: Killer Mike and El-P continue to out-muse each other in a supergroup that somehow seems to get better, louder, and more pertinent since their start in 2013.

videos.title: Esmé Patterson
videos.overview: Esmé Patterson has dropped the banjos and folk from her previous project Paper Bird, and in their place are electric guitars and a backing band worth getting behind.

videos.title: Agnes Obel
videos.overview: Agnes Obel manipulated the Tiny Desk to better suit the deeply alluring and powerful music she brought to us.

videos.title: Little Simz
videos.overview: Little Simz has been compared to Lauryn Hill for her self-reflective wordplay. And though the British lyricist is a relative new-comer, her Tiny Desk performance was poised and confident.

videos.title: Dirty Dozen Brass Band
videos.overview: To celebrate Fat Tuesday, The Dirty Dozen Brass Band brought their euphoric horns to the Tiny Desk for a raucous, joyous set.

videos.title: Ninet
videos.overview: One of Israel's very popular artists may be walking a similar path to early-career Joan Jett — she brought that same intensity to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Maren Morris
videos.overview: One of the newest Grammy winners stops by the Tiny Desk to share her winking, sometimes tongue-in-cheek songs.

videos.title: Tank And The Bangas
videos.overview: Tank And The Bangas' victory lap around the Tiny Desk was momentous, celebratory and deeply touching, with a flair and alchemy of styles that could come from New Orleans.

videos.title: Red Baraat's Holi Celebration
videos.overview: The Brooklyn bhangra band come to the Tiny Desk in celebration of Holi, the Hindu festival of color that welcomes the coming of spring.

videos.title: Sampha
videos.overview: A Tiny Desk Concert as intimate as it gets (that's saying something). Just Sampha, a piano and three heart-wrenching songs that seem to double as coping mechanisms.

videos.title: Delicate Steve
videos.overview: This fierce and lyrical guitar player writes playful instrumental music led by hooky vocals — but there is no voice, just the human-like twang of a glass slide on a guitar.

videos.title: Overcoats
videos.overview: Hana Elion and JJ Mitchell's vibrant vocal harmonies are set against an electronic backdrop that feels spacious and refreshing.

videos.title: Noname
videos.overview: The power of language to penetrate a difficult subject, and the power of performance to share that language, are the gifts Noname brought to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Tash Sultana
videos.overview: It's astonishing to watch Sultana's fluidity on her instrument, like a natural extension of her body. She also plays bass, saxophone, trumpet, flute and more, but kept it "simple" for the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Sinkane
videos.overview: You can hear a great New York jazz band in the rhythms of Sinkane, but you can also hear the influence of Bob Marley and the hypnotic repetition of Sudanese desert sounds.

videos.title: Ljova And The Kontraband
videos.overview: Composer, arranger and viola player Ljova lead his Kontraband to the Tiny Desk for an eclectic swirl of Western classical, jazz, tango and Eastern European and Balkan folk music.

videos.title: Chicano Batman
videos.overview: Chicano Batman comes with a sound that perfectly captures dark lounges, quinceñera dances, car shows and backyard parties.

videos.title: alt-J
videos.overview: There's a self-imposed rule for Tiny Desk Concerts: No artist can visit twice unless there's something wholly different about what they're doing. alt-J was happy to oblige.

videos.title: Antonio Lizana
videos.overview: The traditions of flamenco and jazz are disparate, but in the hands of a few Spanish jazz musicians, these two worlds commingle and find common ground.

videos.title: Avery*Sunshine
videos.overview: The gospel-trained singer showcased why she counts Aretha Franklin and Smokey Robinson as fans.

videos.title: Peter Silberman
videos.overview: A strange condition hushed the life of Peter Silberman, resulting in what may be the quietest Tiny Desk Concert ever.

videos.title: Aimee Mann
videos.overview: "This song is called 'You Never Loved Me' — it's another cheery, optimistic number," says Aimee Mann, introducing the second of four songs in this Tiny Desk Concert.

videos.title: Danilo Brito
videos.overview: Danilo Brito and his band brought their dextrous expression of choro music to the Tiny Desk, a long-established musical style that has its roots in the streets and backyards of Brito's native Brazil.

videos.title: Tim Darcy
videos.overview: Tim Darcy of Montreal band Ought brings his mysterious solo work, from the album Saturday Night, to the Tiny Desk. The record he says, was his chance to “get back to my roots, in my own voice.”

videos.title: Troker
videos.overview: Mexico may not be known for its jazz, but the young lions of Troker are a promising hope to make the country and its capital city a destination.

videos.title: Julia Jacklin
videos.overview: A restrained, whisper-soft Tiny Desk concert from Australian singer-songwriter Julia Jacklin with songs taken from her debut album Don't Let The Kids Win.

videos.title: Gabriel Garzón-Montano
videos.overview: Gabriel Garzón-Montano spent three years writing and recording his beautiful, dense album Jardin -- but for his Tiny Desk visit, he stripped it all down to two elements, the piano and his voice.

videos.title: Royal Thunder
videos.overview: What happens when you ask a hard-rock band to unplug its thunder? It draws power from a raw, desperate vulnerability.

videos.title: Nick Grant
videos.overview: The Atlanta-based MC came through with the flu and coolly earned our praise. How sick is that?

videos.title: Violents & Monica Martin
videos.overview: While her band was on hiatus, Monica Martin joined Jeremy Larson's project Violents, yielding a lush record of electronic pop, translated into a quieted set at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Perfume Genius
videos.overview: The band's long-awaited performance at the Tiny Desk was both beautiful and, at times, intense, featuring three deeply personal songs by frontman Mike Hadreas.

videos.title: Penguin Cafe
videos.overview: Penguin Cafe folds in sounds from around the world and throughout music history — Africa, Kraftwerk, Brazil and Franz Schubert.

videos.title: Tigers Jaw
videos.overview: The duo strips down to acoustic guitar and keyboard for a strikingly intimate set, illuminating their close harmonies that tangle like garlands.

videos.title: Holly Macve
videos.overview: Backed by a suitably low-key band, Macve would sound subtly radiant just about anywhere, from your nearest country bar to the most dreamily lit stage in Twin Peaks.

videos.title: Ravi Coltrane Quartet
videos.overview: Artistic legacy, evolution and studied ease coalesced at this Tiny Desk Concert, with Coltrane offering four interpretations of his and others' works.

videos.title: Helado Negro
videos.overview: Helado Negro ditches his bank of electronics for alto and tenor saxophones, bringing his utterly unique style to a intense, perfectly balanced Tiny Desk Concert.

videos.title: Chance The Rapper
videos.overview: Chance The Rapper, fresh from a 23,000-strong, sold-out show the night before, brought a thoughtful and fresh take to his Tiny Desk concert.

videos.title: Jay Som
videos.overview: Melina Duterte may have played all the instruments on Jay Som's newest record, Everybody Works, but her touring band brought a rougher edge to those silky recordings.

videos.title: Fragile Rock
videos.overview: Fragile Rock is a band that relies on the boogie of The B-52s, the melancholy of The Smiths and the humor of Kermit the Frog. Oh, and they're all puppets.

videos.title: Tuxedo
videos.overview: Tuxedo, the unlikely-on-paper funk-soul duo of Mayer Hawthorne and Jake One, brought a left-of-center sonic approach and a sharp sense of style to their Tiny Desk Concert.

videos.title: Rare Essence
videos.overview: Rare Essence has been bringing go-go to the world since 1976 — the group brought that pedigree, and the genre's massive meld of funk, rhythm and blues and soul, to this raucous hometown Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Albin Lee Meldau
videos.overview: Albin Lee Meldau possesses a thunderous, deeply affecting voice, which he uses to tell some utterly dark, but demonstrably cathartic, tales.

videos.title: The Shins
videos.overview: James Mercer, the emotional and creative heart of The Shins, gives a moving performance at the Tiny Desk, with two new songs and a classic from the band's 2003 album Chutes Too Narrow.

videos.title: Aldous Harding
videos.overview: Intensity in songs often expresses itself as volume – a loud guitar, a scream, a piercing synth line. But in the case of Aldous Harding it's in the spaces, the pauses, and her unique delivery.

videos.title: Diet Cig
videos.overview: Diet Cig's songs crackle like Pop Rocks, but with a confrontational honesty and striking gravity — and on top of Bob Boilen's desk.

videos.title: Maggie Rogers
videos.overview: The rising pop star performs three of her best-known songs, including a sweet solo take on her career-making “Alaska.”

videos.title: ALA.NI
videos.overview: ALA.NI captures and conveys a reverent love of early-20th-century music, while injecting those sounds with charisma and charm well suited for any era.

videos.title: DJ Premier & The Badder Band
videos.overview: One of hip-hop's most revered producers brings his songs to life behind the Tiny Desk, with the help of a four-piece band.

videos.title: Jason Isbell
videos.overview: The Alabama singer-songwriter and his band perform three songs from The Nashville Sound, but their set includes a few surprises, too.

videos.title: Jidenna
videos.overview: The Nigerian-American MC and his band perform three reworked selections from Jidenna's impeccable debut album, The Chief.

videos.title: Frances Cone
videos.overview: The Brooklyn-based band crafts infectious pop music that builds dramatically before giving way to a quiet calm.

videos.title: Bleachers
videos.overview: Jack Antonoff re-arranged three songs from his band's latest album, Gone Now, for the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: L.A. Salami
videos.overview: The story songs and poetry of Lookman Adekunle Salami, who writes and records as L.A. Salami, recall the brilliant and epic ramblings of Bob Dylan.

videos.title: Snail Mail
videos.overview: Snail Mail's sleepy songs have a way of waking you up. Watch the band perform music from its quietly stunning Habit EP, plus a new song played solo by Lindsey Jordan.

videos.title: SsingSsing
videos.overview: It's safe to say this Korean, cross-dressing rock band looks and sounds like no one who's ever performed at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Bomba Estereo
videos.overview: Bomba Estereo is not known as a hushed band. Member Simon Mejia said this Tiny Desk performance was the group's quietest, a stripped-down treatment that illustrates the inherent quality of the music.

videos.title: Steve Martin And The Steep Canyon Rangers
videos.overview: It's hard to think of an artist who's brought more joy to more people, across more generations — and in more ways — than Steve Martin.

videos.title: Chronixx
videos.overview: The Jamaican reggae star proudly carries the torch of his country's roots reggae legends.

videos.title: Dawg Yawp
videos.overview: Welcome the world of Dawg Yawp, the musical concoction of Rob Keenan and Tyler Randall, where drones and toy pianos are likely to collide with heavy metal electronics and a well-placed melody.

videos.title: Paramore
videos.overview: Paramore captures the moment between rapture and its comedown. Watch the band rearrange songs from its sparkling pop album After Laughter.

videos.title: Landlady
videos.overview: Landlady's music is more than sonic exploration, it's an adventure. The songs can feel a bit drugged-out – a bit high and full of curiosity – but never overly intoxicated or out-of-touch.

videos.title: Randy Newman
videos.overview: Watch the six-time Grammy winner go solo behind the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Hanson
videos.overview: Isaac, Taylor and Zac Hanson just celebrated their 25th anniversary as a band. To celebrate, watch them perform three of their post-“MMMBop” career highlights.

videos.title: Thundercat
videos.overview: Thundercat is willing and able to shape-shift to fit into just about any box you show him, but he won't stay in there for long.

videos.title: The Perceptionists
videos.overview: Watch hip-hop veterans Mr. Lif and Akrobatik team up behind the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Shabazz Palaces
videos.overview: Hip-hop's otherworldly lot touches down on Bob Boilen's desk for some Afrofuturistic mind travel.

videos.title: Japanese Breakfast
videos.overview: For this Tiny Desk concert, Japanese Breakfast's Michelle Zauner replaced her gauzy synths with a string quartet. The result is something to behold.

videos.title: Natalia LaFourcade
videos.overview: The Grammy-nominated singer's Tiny Desk is an ode to a magical time in Mexican popular music.

videos.title: The Roots Feat. Bilal
videos.overview: Yes, it happened. Black Thought, Questlove and the entire crew packed in behind the Tiny Desk to perform a new song called “It Ain't Fair.”

videos.title: Gracie and Rachel
videos.overview: Gracie And Rachel mix piano pop with darker, classic violin arrangements to make songs full of mystery and tension. They're joined in this Tiny Desk performance by percussionist Richard Watts.

videos.title: Nate Smith + KINFOLK
videos.overview: The drums take center stage at this Tiny Desk. Watch veteran jazz percussionist Nate Smith dazzle the NPR audience in a transfixing performance.

videos.title: Wyclef Jean
videos.overview: The hip-hop statesman walked through our doors greeting and charming anyone within arm's reach. Once in front of an audience, he was in attack mode, including a unique rendition of his signature hit.

videos.title: Ani DiFranco
videos.overview: With the help of a backing band that includes Ivan Neville and Jenny Scheinman, the iconic singer-songwriter plays three songs from across her tough and uncompromising career.

videos.title: The Mynabirds
videos.overview: Singer Laura Burhenn is joined by Jessica Lea Mayfield and the Umoja Choir for songs inspired by the political and cultural upheaval of 2016.

videos.title: Aminé
videos.overview: The Portland artist with the most mispronounced name in hip-hop puts on an unforgettable performance.

videos.title: Now, Now
videos.overview: The band has new tools in its arsenal, but even in a stripped-down Tiny Desk performance, its focus on tiny moments between people just outside of love is as sharp as ever.

videos.title: Benjamin Booker
videos.overview: Benjamin Booker has a deeply tender voice that, at times, can feel like a whisper But it always cuts to the heart.

videos.title: Billy Corgan
videos.overview: Billy Corgan, complicated frontman of The Smashing Pumpkins, has had a tumultuous decade-and-a-half. His visit to the Tiny Desk, with a string quartet backing him, was anything but.

videos.title: Ledisi
videos.overview: In person, the master R&B vocalist impresses not just with her exquisite artistry, but with her radiant spirit of contentment and grace. Just ask her makeup artist.

videos.title: David Greilsammer
videos.overview: With a knack for cunning juxtapositions, the adventurous pianist stitches together a baroque sonata, a slice of French serenity and a quirky portrait of a mysterious barn owl.

videos.title: Phoebe Bridgers
videos.overview: Her songs come laden with finely detailed observations about hypnotherapy, Jeffrey Dahmer and everything in between. They receive a languid, impeccably-phrased performance at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Moses Sumney
videos.overview: The Los-Angeles-based force of nature, one of the most inspired talents of today, shows off a spontaneous side at (and around) the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Walter Martin
videos.overview: Best known for his role with The Walkmen, as a solo artist he makes unabashedly joyful, sweetly innocent and playful music. And only he would arrive with a barbershop quartet.

videos.title: Ted Leo
videos.overview: Leo's work has, more often than not through the decades, addressed an anxious world, growing and shifting with it and with its listeners. Seven years after his last solo album, he's turned inwards.

videos.title: King Krule
videos.overview: King Krule, the musical project of English singer, songwriter and rapper, Archy Marshall, brings its twisted, woozy tones to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Courtney Barnett and Kurt Vile
videos.overview: The two singers, songwriters and guitarists bring out the adolescence in each other, poking jabs, goofing around and having fun at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Tyler, The Creator
videos.overview: Tyler, The Creator performs three songs from his latest album Flower Boy -- and pulls off (at least) two Tiny Desk firsts in the process, while maturing beyond his class-clown image (mostly).

videos.title: Cigarettes After Sex
videos.overview: This comes close to the quietest Tiny Desk Concert we've ever had. The music Cigarettes After Sex makes is incredibly hushed. It's a sound so minimal it barely exists.

videos.title: This Is The Kit
videos.overview: Effortless storytelling is at the heart of This Is The Kit. And the stories the band's only permanent member, Kate Stables, weaves are profound but sweet with a tone that quietly reels you in.

videos.title: Hanson For The Holidays
videos.overview: Frantic time-lapse set decoration. An intrusive snow machine. Ugly holiday sweaters. It's time to hunker down and soak up a raucous and reverent Christmas party, courtesy of Hanson.

videos.title: Open Mike Eagle
videos.overview: The indie rap denizen behind one of 2017's most inventive albums came to the nation's capital to represent all the Brick Body Kids who Still Daydream.

videos.title: Lo Moon
videos.overview: The LA band's signature sound is intimate and demonstrative, haunting yet uplifting, an old-fashioned rock beat under glimmering guitar and keys. And at the Tiny Desk, it was at ease.

videos.title: The Weather Station
videos.overview: One of the joys of listening to The Weather station is the tension and release in the group's enchanting music. It's what made the band's most recent album one of Bob Boilen's favorite of 2017.

videos.title: Julien Baker
videos.overview: Julien Baker's Turn Out The Lights brought her much-deserved critical acclaim and wider attention in 2017. Before its release we asked her to make a rare return to the Tiny Desk for something special.

videos.title: Daniil Trifonov
videos.overview: Watch the young Russian musician, who The Times of London calls “the most astounding pianist of our age,” play a smart, Chopin-focused concert on a grand piano, precisely wedged behind the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Artists From The 'Take Me To The River' Tour
videos.overview: More than a dozen artists gather behind the Tiny Desk to celebrate Memphis soul in a joyful, triumphant performance.

videos.title: AHI
videos.overview: The Ontario-based singer has a gruff but sweet voice with openly honest words behind soulful tunes of hope.

videos.title: The Lemon Twigs
videos.overview: Brothers Brian and Michael D'Addario seem like they beamed into the Tiny Desk from the year 1971, untouched by the 21st century.

videos.title: Amadou and Mariam
videos.overview: The Malian musicians, who've been playing together for nearly 40 years, bring some of the most lyrical melodies and joyful sounds we've ever had at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: St. Vincent
videos.overview: The singer performed at the Tiny Desk without a warmup or soundcheck, with just her acoustic guitar and un-amplified voice, letting the wordplay in her songs shine through.

videos.title: George Clinton & The P-Funk All Stars
videos.overview: George Clinton brought his family, both immediate and extended, to the Tiny Desk for a set of classic cosmic slop.

videos.title: Barbara Hannigan
videos.overview: Eavesdrop on a beautiful recital of German songs from fin de siècle Vienna, when music was transitioning from the swells of romanticism to the uncharted waters of modernism.

videos.title: Jamila Woods
videos.overview: In three songs celebrating black ancestry and self-love, Woods demonstrated just how adept she is at creating songs rich with philosophical meaning that also move and groove.

videos.title: Alice Smith
videos.overview: The beloved singer-songwriter premiered three new songs while turning NPR's headquarters into a Harlem speakeasy.

videos.title: Vicente García
videos.overview: This under-the-radar singer from the Dominican Republic is starting to turn some heads. You'll see why in this Tiny Desk performance.

videos.title: Hurray For The Riff Raff
videos.overview: The music of Hurray For The Riff Raff builds bridges, unites people and forms communities. It's a spirit singer Alynda Segarra and the rest of the band bring to this memorable Tiny Desk performance.

videos.title: Ibeyi
videos.overview: Lisa-Kaindé and Naomi Díaz never fail to mesmerize. Watch the twin sisters perform a four-song set at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: The Crossrhodes
videos.overview: The Crossrhodes showed up to the Tiny Desk with game faces on, bringing with it a locally cultivated, globally appreciated energy.

videos.title: Marlon Williams
videos.overview: Marlon Williams has a heart-stopping voice, is in love with a good, traditional blues or country tune, and writes songs about vampires and horror films.

videos.title: Nick Hakim
videos.overview: The music of Nick Hakim occupies a space and time that feels out of this world, with songs that explore the quietude of inner thoughts.

videos.title: Betsayda Machado y Parranda El Clavo
videos.overview: The Afro-Venezuelan collective brings the boisterous parranda sound to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Big Daddy Kane
videos.overview: One of the greatest to ever bless the mic treated the Tiny Desk audience to an office block party.

videos.title: August Greene (Common, Robert Glasper, Karriem Riggins)
videos.overview: August Greene, Common's new trio with Robert Glasper and Karriem Riggins, brought some special guest vocalists to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Vagabon
videos.overview: Laetitia Tamko, the artist known as Vagabon, is a 25-year-old, Cameroon-born musician with a big, tenor voice just bursting with new musical ideas.

videos.title: Lee Ann Womack
videos.overview: The Nashville star brought some good old country music stories to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Roy Ayers
videos.overview: Watch the 77-year-old jazz-funk icon perform “Everybody Loves The Sunshine” (and more) at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Anna Meredith
videos.overview: Out of nearly 700 performances at the Tiny Desk over the past decade, this one by British composer Anna Meredith is one of the most exhilarating.

videos.title: Big K.R.I.T.
videos.overview: The Mississippi rapper paid homage to his grandmother and performed songs from his new album 4eva Is a Mighty Long Time.

videos.title: Alex Clare
videos.overview: Clare's songs ask listeners to probe their own emotions through the lens of life’s bigger pictures. His visit to Bob Boilen’s desk is the perfect setting to bask in the power of his voice.

videos.title: Kuinka
videos.overview: Each year we get thousands of submissions for our annual Tiny Desk contest. Seattle's Kuinka was one of last year's entrants. While they didn't win, we loved them so much we invited them to come play.

videos.title: John Prine
videos.overview: For more than 45 years, the legendary John Prine has written some of the most powerful lyrics in the American music canon. He brings some of his best to this unforgettable Tiny Desk performance.

videos.title: Raul Midón
videos.overview: Raul Midón brought nothing but a guitar and his voice to an extended Tiny Desk set of dense, breathtaking jazz and soul textures.

videos.title: Cornelius
videos.overview: Cornelius' Keigo Oyamada deconstructs and reassembles music like it's a neon cubist-pop sculpture. On a rare U.S. tour, the Japanese band brought its complex cool to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Väsen
videos.overview: The Swedish trio brought a 30-string sonic blast to the Tiny Desk, performing on 12-string guitar, viola and the nyckelharpa (a fiddle with keys — think 15th century keytar).

videos.title: Jenny And The Mexicats
videos.overview: Sometimes frenetic, sometimes slow and luxurious, the grooves the band creates are the perfect cushion for Jenny Ball's impassioned singing and engaging stage presence.

videos.title: I'm With Her
videos.overview: Aoife O'Donovan, Sarah Jarosz and Sara Watkins are bound by a love for bluegrass, chamber music, jazz, storytelling and singing.

videos.title: Masta Ace
videos.overview: The Juice Crew legend brought his biggest hit, "Born To Roll," and a heartfelt recollection of his personal journey to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Robin Olson
videos.overview: Hear the elusive avant-garde pianist debut a new piece, etched in shimmering chords and dark, lamenting octaves.

videos.title: Dee Dee Bridgewater
videos.overview: Bridgewater connects with her roots, her birthplace and the town she's loved all her life, with a set of songs from Memphis.

videos.title: Dan Auerbach
videos.overview: The guitarist and singer for The Black Keys and The Arcs brings his Easy Eye Sound Revue to the Tiny Desk, recalling a time and sound from the '60s when southern R&B, including Nashville, was a force.

videos.title: Rhye
videos.overview: See the band perform a rare evening Tiny Desk concert, illuminated by flickering lights

videos.title: Lara Bello
videos.overview: Flamenco, jazz and classical share the stage in this Tiny Desk from one of our favorite Spanish composers.

videos.title: Tyler Childers
videos.overview: Tyler Childers writes songs about hard lives and hard love with direct heart and a soulful Kentucky drawl.

videos.title: Jorge Drexler
videos.overview: The Uruguayan singer-songwriter is one of the finest lyricists operating today. Watch his stunning performance behind the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: The Breeders
videos.overview: The Breeders' dreamy scuzz sounds wiser and more frazzled at the Tiny Desk, featuring the same lineup behind the band's breakout, 1993 album Last Splash.

videos.title: O.C.
videos.overview: The veteran Brooklyn rapper was an underground star during hip-hop's golden era. At the Tiny Desk, O.C. made it clear that he hasn't lost his edge.

videos.title: John Moreland
videos.overview: When you hear John Moreland's sweet voice, it's hard to believe he spent years singing in punk, metal-core and hardcore bands. He plays acoustic guitar now, but his songs are still full of passion.

videos.title: Logan Richardson
videos.overview: Hear a triumphant fusion of jazz, rock and blues that moves with momentum and fresh anticipation. Logan Richardson plays with a lyrical intensity that is both focused and free.

videos.title: Superorganism
videos.overview: The multinational band of theatrically fun and talented musicians in Superorganism mix melody and mischievous with almost Seussian folly.

videos.title: ÌFÉ
videos.overview: ÌFÉ isn't playing anything new. In fact, the band takes on something quite old: ritual Afro-Caribbean music that takes a lifetime to absorb and master.

videos.title: Bedouine
videos.overview: Bedouine is Azniv Korkejian, a singer and guitarist who echoes sounds from the 1960's North American folk songwriters, but with vocal inflections closer to Leonard Cohen than to Joni Mitchell.

videos.title: GZA & The Soul Rebels
videos.overview: Most rap fans would name RZA as the head of the Wu-Tang Clan. But Wu purists know that GZA, or The Genius, is the crew's unspoken elder statesman.

videos.title: Darlingside
videos.overview: Even if the world came to an end, there's still beauty and hope in all of us and in song. That about sums up the wistful mystery that is the music of Darlingside.

videos.title: Gordi
videos.overview: In three songs from Reservoir, Gordi keeps her voice both unadorned and centered within warm, cool arrangements that include piano, guitar, pedal steel, a harmonium named Barbara, and more.

videos.title: Bela Fleck And Abigail Washburn
videos.overview: Bela Fleck and Abigail Washburn are two American musical treasures. This husband-and-wife banjo duo write original tunes steeped in the roots of folk music.

videos.title: Naia Izumi
videos.overview: The winner of this year's Tiny Desk Contest makes his official debut behind the desk.

videos.title: Khruangbin
videos.overview: This trio from Houston, Texas makes trance-inducing music heavily inspired by 1960s and '70s funk and soul from, of all places, Thailand.

videos.title: Partner
videos.overview: The dream of the '90s is alive in this Canadian rock band.

videos.title: The Band's Visit
videos.overview: Tony Shalhoub, Katrina Lenk and the cast of the Tony-nominated play The Band's Visit marked the first Broadway performance at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Juanes & Mon Laferte
videos.overview: The Colombian pop star and Chilean rising star brought their duet tour to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Ill Camille
videos.overview: The Los Angeles rapper and Kendrick Lamar collaborator performed four songs from her excellent album, Heirloom.

videos.title: Third Coast Percussion
videos.overview: Watch the Chicago-based ensemble conjure otherworldly sounds from steel pipes, tuned cowbells and a bowl that sings.

videos.title: Trouble Funk
videos.overview: We squeezed 12 go-go musicians behind the Tiny Desk. Watch what ensued.

videos.title: Tom Misch
videos.overview: This 22-year-old Brit has soul for days.

videos.title: Daniel Caesar
videos.overview: Watch the R&B star-in-the-making perform three songs, including a guest appearance by H.E.R.

videos.title: Grace VanderWaal
videos.overview: The 14-year-old singer who signed to Columbia after winning America's Got Talent, dazzles the Tiny Desk with her breathtaking voice.

videos.title: MILCK
videos.overview: The one-woman riot who made headlines during the inaugural Women's March On Washington visits the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Jorja Smith
videos.overview: Watch the rising U.K. star perform intimate renditions of "Blue Lights," "On My Mind" and "Teenage Fantasy" with a full band.

videos.title: GoldLink
videos.overview: The D.C. rapper brought quite the crew to his Tiny Desk performance.

videos.title: Yissy García & Bandancha
videos.overview: Come for one of Havana's most talented acts. Stay for García's incredible mohawk.

videos.title: Khalid
videos.overview: Watch the 20-year-old star perform acoustic versions of "Location," "Saved" and "Young Dumb & Broke."

videos.title: The Messthetics
videos.overview: The bassist and drummer from D.C.'s pioneering punk band Fugazi join guitarist Anthony Pirog for a set of thrilling, sometimes loud and frenetic instrumentals.

videos.title: From The Top
videos.overview: A handful of teenagers, and a 12-year-old violinist, from the radio show From the Top, give sparkling performances, proving there's a bright future for classical music.

videos.title: Rakim
videos.overview: Watch the New York rap icon perform "Paid In Full" and "Know The Ledge," as well as a new song for Marvel's Luke Cage, at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Dave Matthews
videos.overview: The star sheds his band for a warm, winning, utterly game, happily overstuffed five-song performance of songs from across his long career.

videos.title: Golden Dawn Arkestra
videos.overview: Join the "Children of the Sun" - or sit back and enjoy the spectacle - in this Tiny Desk experience.

videos.title: PJ Morton
videos.overview: New Orleans' native son brought his musical Gumbo — and a 10-piece orchestra — to the Tiny Desk for some well-seasoned soul and a lesson in creative freedom.

videos.title: Frédéric Yonnet With Special Guest Dave Chappelle
videos.overview: Yonnet is a magician on the harmonica. You'll see why he's performed with Stevie Wonder, Prince and Ed Sheeran.

videos.title: Rev. Sekou And The Seal Breakers
videos.overview: Rev. Sekou and the Seal Breakers gave one of the most rousing Tiny Desks we've ever had, opening with one question: "Do you want to get free?"

videos.title: Mumu Fresh Feat. Black Thought & DJ Dummy
videos.overview: Occasionally a new voice emerges so rich in experience that the only way to describe it is old soul.

videos.title: The Midnight Hour
videos.overview: A Tribe Called Quest's Ali Shaheed Muhammad and composer Adrian Younge brought their Luke Cage-inspired collaboration to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Ólafur Arnalds
videos.overview: The Icelandic composer is joined by two "ghost" pianists, making mysterious and memorable music at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: The King's Singers
videos.overview: The storied vocal ensemble brings close harmony singing to a diverse set list that includes a Beatles tune and a bawdy madrigal from the 1500s.

videos.title: Lalah Hathaway
videos.overview: The veteran singer showcases her soaring powerfully expressive voice in a performance that bridges several generations of classic soul.

videos.title: Flasher
videos.overview: The precise serrations of Washington, D.C. band Flasher get softened for a visit to the Tiny Desk — their vocals, normally side-by-side rushing electric instruments, get the center stage treatment.

videos.title: The Del McCoury Band
videos.overview: Del McCoury has been performing, and updating, his take on bluegrass for some 60 years. At the Tiny Desk, he brought three traveling songs and some good yarns to share from his ample time on the road.

videos.title: Haley Heynderickx
videos.overview: One of our favorite new artists of 2018 visits the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Mac Miller
videos.overview: Mac Miller reflects on his journey's peaks and valleys in a boisterous set of songs from Swimming, featuring special guest Thundercat on "What's the Use?"

videos.title: DAWN
videos.overview: DAWN has a breathless enthusiasm for shape-shifting pop music. She strips three songs to just the essentials, illuminating the impeccable songwriting behind her wild combination of sounds.

videos.title: Tower Of Power
videos.overview: Even from its beginnings in late-'60s Oakland, the band has always stood out. Fifty years later, its devotion to classic horn-driven soul remains unmatched, its passion and precision unchanged.

videos.title: Erykah Badu
videos.overview: The singer's performance at the Tiny Desk was an almost spiritual experience, leaving many at the NPR Music offices in awe.

videos.title: Yo-Yo Ma
videos.overview: Watch the 19-time Grammy winner return to his lifelong passion for J.S. Bach, playing music from the Cello Suites and offering advice on the art of incremental learning.

videos.title: Camp Cope
videos.overview: The Australian band uses tiny moments of introspection to illuminate life's bewildering, terrifying, isolating aspects — especially as they apply to women.

videos.title: Dermot Kennedy
videos.overview: Backed for the first time ever by members of the Howard Gospel Choir, the Irish singer-songwriter shows off a voice built to fill stadiums in more ways than one.

videos.title: T.I.
videos.overview: In the fifteen years since he released Trap Muzik, Tip Harris has reinvented himself a thousand times over. But the stories he recounts from that era make his Tiny Desk a memorable one.

videos.title: Tech N9ne Feat. Krizz Kaliko
videos.overview: Two of Kansas City's finest — and indie hip-hop's trailblazers — deliver a dose of Strange Music.

videos.title: George Li
videos.overview: Watch the young Harvard grad dispatch some of the most "knuckle-busting" piano repertoire with uncommon panache and precision.

videos.title: Kalbells
videos.overview: The band makes life-affirming music that singer Kalmia Traver created over the past few years, filled with the triumph of being cancer free.

videos.title: Jupiter & Okwess
videos.overview: Jupiter Bokondji and his band Okwess play music that feels both African and American, with Jupiter's early musical tastes inspired by The Jackson 5, James Brown and the sounds of Motown.

videos.title: Hobo Johnson
videos.overview: While this Sacramento, Calif. band didn't win this year's Tiny Desk contest, their video entry, for the song "Peach Scones," was among the more memorable we've ever seen.

videos.title: GoGo Penguin
videos.overview: This trio has become a reference point of their own for new school instrumentalists, a coveted achievement for any jazz group, though their appeal stretches far outside the jazz ecosystem.

videos.title: Smif-N-Wessun
videos.overview: Brooklyn-bred hip-hop duo Smif-N-Wessun – consisting of partners in rhyme, Steele and Tek – illuminated the Tiny Desk with their signature, 80-proof poetry: straight, no chaser.

videos.title: Julie Byrne
videos.overview: Julie Byrne's transporting music can turn the ordinary into the extraordinary.

videos.title: Anthony Roth Costanzo
videos.overview: Watch the ambitious countertenor sing music that spans more than 250 years, connecting the dots between David Byrne, George Frideric Handel and Philip Glass.

videos.title: Cécile McLorin Salvant
videos.overview: The jazz singer, who used to be into radical feminist punk, now composes and sings beautiful jazz ballads.

videos.title: Saba
videos.overview: Before embarking on a tour of Australia and Asia, the Chicago native brought the squad that helped make Care For Me one of 2018's best — along with a very special guest.

videos.title: Cory Henry & The Funk Apostles
videos.overview: Henry and his band would have sounded right at home on Stax Records in the '70s — no small accomplishment. Watch them perform three funky, soulful jams.

videos.title: Big Boi
videos.overview: The OutKast star performs "So Fresh, So Clean," "The Way You Move" and his solo single "All Night" with the help of singer Sleepy Brown and an eight-member backing band.

videos.title: Café Tacvba
videos.overview: The pioneering Mexican band recreates the adventurous musical energy of their massive stadium shows behind Bob Boilen's desk.

videos.title: Florence + the Machine
videos.overview: "I'm sorry I'm shy," Florence Welch told the crowd of NPR family and friends gathered for her Tiny Desk performance. "If this was a big gig, I'd probably be climbing all over here and running around."

videos.title: Alfredo Rodríguez
videos.overview: The Cuban pianist thrilled the NPR office with an intense performance that was as melodic as it was rhythmic.

videos.title: Chromeo
videos.overview: The self-proclaimed "Funklordz" normally perform as a duo, but played with a live band for the first time at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Cautious Clay
videos.overview: The charismatic singer and saxophonist brought a group of longtime friends to play a warm, thoughtful and chill set at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Jim James
videos.overview: A single voice can send a powerful message - and that's just what Jim James did at the Tiny Desk, with just his voice and an acoustic guitar.

videos.title: Liniker e os Caramelows
videos.overview: Liniker e os Caramelows are from Brazil but steeped in the tradition of soul from here in the U.S. Watching this performance is to witness a spell being cast, note-by-note.

videos.title: Nicholas Payton Trio
videos.overview: After back-to-back performances in South Africa, Argentina, Chile and New York, Payton hit the Tiny Desk, where he dazzled the audience, simultaneously playing his trumpet and a Fender Rhodes.

videos.title: Pedro The Lion
videos.overview: No matter how dark or disastrous, there's always been an undercurrent of grace to the music of David Bazan. He returns to his Pedro the Lion moniker for this memorable Tiny Desk performance.

videos.title: Half Waif
videos.overview: The band's songs, stripped here to their essence, are particularly peaceful and calm — and sometimes chilling.

videos.title: Bernie And The Believers Feat. Essence
videos.overview: The story of Bernie and the Believers is the story of Bernie Dalton's diagnosis of Lou Gehrig's disease and compassionate friends making his dream come true and his songs come to life.

videos.title: Boygenius
videos.overview: Julien Baker, Lucy Dacus and Phoebe Bridgers are all Tiny Desk alumae, but here they play together at NPR for the first time as boygenius, one of this year's best surprises.

videos.title: dvsn
videos.overview: The Toronto-based R&B duo bathed the Tiny Desk in vibrant blue, purple and orange light to make it feel more like a concert hall.

videos.title: The Innocence Mission
videos.overview: The Innocence Mission, ever the most careful cultivators of quiet, encouraged us to come closer, to discover the "thing beautiful enough" in the moment it's delivered.

videos.title: Joey Alexander
videos.overview: No one in the NPR offices could have imagined how remarkable this 15-year old pianist would be at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Dirty Projectors
videos.overview: The band takes its quirks of production, rhythm and rhyme and brilliantly arranges them to work behind the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Wu-Tang Clan
videos.overview: The Clan celebrates its 25th anniversary with an old-school cipher at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: H.E.R.
videos.overview: The singer stuns in her second appearance at the Tiny Desk, showcasing not only her vocal mastery, but her skills as a captivating multi-instrumentalist.

videos.title: Harold López-Nussa Trio
videos.overview: Cuban pianist Harold López-Nussa, along with his brother Ruy on drums and bassist Gaston Joya, deliver a set of danceable jazz explorations rooted in Afro-Cuban musical traditions to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Amy Grant
videos.overview: Amy Grant maps her fabulous, four-decade career with some of her coziest and heartfelt Christmas songs, not to mention a delightful version of "Jingle Bells."

videos.title: Miguel Zenón feat. Spektral Quartet
videos.overview: The saxophonist is a big thinker whose mesmerizing compositions chronicle the music of his native Puerto Rico with the help of an adventurous jazz quartet.

videos.title: Buddy
videos.overview: The preacher's son from Compton brought his flair for the dramatic, and an air of rebellion, to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Carolina Eyck and Clarice Jensen
videos.overview: Carolina Eyck, the first artist to bring a theremin to the Tiny Desk, plays the air with the kind of lyrical phrasing and "fingered" articulation that takes a special kind of virtuosity.

videos.title: Aaron Lee Tasjan
videos.overview: Aaron Lee Tasjan arrived in an ascot and mustard-colored shirt, sporting red, round sunglasses and mutton chops. It was a fashionable nod to the psych-pop and rock sound he brought to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Nate Wood - fOUR
videos.overview: The multi-instrumentalist says he only wishes he had more limbs; but Wood still manages to simultaneously play a bass guitar, keys and drums, all while singing into a wearable microphone.

videos.title: Stella Donnelly
videos.overview: Watch the Australian singer-songwriter perform three new songs from her upcoming full-length debut, Beware of the Dogs.

videos.title: Blood Orange
videos.overview: This Blood Orange Tiny Desk is a beautifully conceived concert showing off the craft and care that has made Devonté Hynes a groundbreaking producer and songwriter.

videos.title: Cat Power
videos.overview: Chan Marshall and her band perform a brisk and beautifully orchestrated medley of Cat Power songs: "Wanderer," "Woman" and 2006's "The Moon."

videos.title: Kurt Vile
videos.overview: Kurt Vile and his musical mate, Rob Laakso casually lose themselves in complex guitar lines that are effortlessly beautiful and lyrical.

videos.title: Lau Noah
videos.overview: There's a magical aura that surrounds Lau Noah as she sits behind the Tiny Desk and unspools thought-provoking story-songs.

videos.title: Mountain Man
videos.overview: The voices of Amelia Meath, Molly Erin Sarlé and Alexandra Sauser-Monnig come together behind the Tiny Desk, with songs that conjure a simpler life: dogs, friends, moonlight or skinny dipping.

videos.title: Scott Mulvahill
videos.overview: Scott Mulvahill has been trying to win the Tiny Desk Contest for each of its four years. And while he's never won, we all loved him so much we had to invite him to play.

videos.title: The Pedrito Martinez Group
videos.overview: The Afro-Cuban percussionist mesmerizes with his almost otherworldly talent on congas.

videos.title: Natalie Prass
videos.overview: Decked out in matching, cobalt blue outfits, the singer and her band had a clear vision: If you want to overcome the times, find strength in numbers.

videos.title: Zaytoven
videos.overview: The Atlanta trap super-producer and son of a preacher man saved the day with a soulful Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Phony Ppl
videos.overview: The Brooklynites stand out for their inventive and seamless blend of jazz, R&B and hip-hop.

videos.title: Meg Myers
videos.overview: Myers replaces her album's roaring electric guitars and electronics with a pulsing string quartet, piano and brushed drums — and uncorks a cover of Kate Bush's "Running Up That Hill."

videos.title: Leikeli47
videos.overview: The artist came to the Tiny Desk masked up, as always, the better to catch a glimpse of her soul.

videos.title: Kaia Kater
videos.overview: Multi-hyphenate artist Kaia Kater uses the architecture of roots music, which she studied in West Virginia, to establish a simultaneous dialogue with both the present moment and her own past.

videos.title: Nao
videos.overview: The U.K.-based singer-songwriter takes the Tiny Desk on a cosmic journey through her Saturn return.

videos.title: Alejandro Escovedo
videos.overview: The veteran rocker and a backup band from Italy play songs from their album The Crossing, chronicling an American Dream of rock and roll and Beat poetry.

videos.title: &More (Chill Moody & Donn T)
videos.overview: Philadelphia Rapper Chill Moody and singer Donn T, along with their crew known as &More, were one of the standout entrants in last year's Tiny Desk Contest. They bring a message of hope and love.

videos.title: Andrea Cruz
videos.overview: The singer from Puerto Rico is part of a movement on the island that emphasizes largely acoustic instruments and a folk-based approach to interpreting life before and after the hurricane of 2017.

videos.title: Weezer
videos.overview: Performing unplugged, the band forgoes its usual meticulousness in favor of a shaggy, entirely acoustic mix of new songs and '90s-era deep cuts.

videos.title: Courtney Marie Andrews
videos.overview: It was a day when sunlight drenched the office and the songs of heart from Courtney Marie Andrews felt right at home.

videos.title: Georgia Anne Muldrow
videos.overview: The R&B singer from Los Angeles is all about showing and spreading love.

videos.title: Karine Polwart Trio
videos.overview: Scottish singer, songwriter and essayist Karine Polwart seldom comes stateside, eschewing air travel to reduce her carbon footprint. But on a rare, recent visit, she stopped in D.C. for a Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Gary Clark Jr.
videos.overview: These three songs, from Clark's incendiary new album This Land, roar with the assurance and force of a showman at the top of his game.

videos.title: Theodore
videos.overview: The music of Theodore is dark and transformative, with the kind of spare elegance you can hear in Sigur Rós or Pink Floyd.

videos.title: The Calidore String Quartet
videos.overview: The Calidore String Quartet confirms that the centuries-old formula — two violins, a viola and a cello — is still very much alive and evolving.

videos.title: Better Oblivion Community Center
videos.overview: Tiny Desk alums Conor Oberst and Phoebe Bridgers surprised us all with their stunning collaboration this year as Better Oblivion Community Center. Together they radiate joy at the desk.

videos.title: Toro Y Moi
videos.overview: Toro y Moi loses the voice processing, synths and other heavy effects for a stripped-down acoustic set at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Laraaji
videos.overview: Laraaji is best known to some for his ambient work with Brian Eno in the late '70s. He brings his meditative calm to the Tiny Desk in this hypnotic performance.

videos.title: Thou
videos.overview: This is probably the quietest you'll ever hear the first metal band to play the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Ohmme
videos.overview: These classically trained artists fill the NPR Music offices with shrieking, rhythmic noise that redefines what an electric guitar can do.

videos.title: Magos Herrera and Brooklyn Rider
videos.overview: Watch what happens when the smoky-voiced jazz singer from Mexico conspires with an adventuresome string quartet for songs steeped in Latin American traditions.

videos.title: Ensemble Signal Plays Jonny Greenwood
videos.overview: Watch members of the New York-based group give the world premiere video performances of two recent pieces by Radiohead guitarist and composer Jonny Greenwood.

videos.title: Jeremy Dutcher
videos.overview: There is no one making music like this 27-year-old, classically trained opera tenor and pianist. Watch and see why.

videos.title: Lucky Daye
videos.overview: Hailing from New Orleans with a love of sticky, bass-bumping funk, Lucky brought along a 10-person band, including a quartet of horns, to capture the full flavor of his debut album Painted.

videos.title: LADAMA
videos.overview: The group unites sounds from Brazil, Colombia and Venezuela, with a dash of New York City thrown in.

videos.title: Quinn Christopherson
videos.overview: Quinn and his musical partner, guitarist and singer Nick Carpenter, arrived from the cool of Anchorage to the swelter of D.C. and performed with remarkable confidence and grace.

videos.title: Tomberlin
videos.overview: Tomberlin is the daughter of a Baptist pastor, grew up singing in the church and, since her teens, has questioned her own beliefs in God and faith. Her songs are delicate and vulnerable.

videos.title: Sesame Street
videos.overview: Big Bird, Bert and Ernie, Elmo, Grover, Rosita, Count von Count, Abby Cadabby, Cookie Monster and other surprise guests gather at NPR's headquarters to celebrate 50 years of love, learning and joy.

videos.title: Foxing
videos.overview: Foxing is at the forefront of an emo revival, heavily influenced by late-'90s and early 2000s groups like Sunny Day Real Estate and American Football.

videos.title: IDLES
videos.overview: The British madmen brought fury, cathartic rage and deep thoughts to the Tiny Desk for one of the loudest, most raucous performances in memory.

videos.title: Imogen Heap
videos.overview: Imogen Heap takes us through her many musical talents, from her Frou Frou musical partner, Guy Sigsworth — and their first new song in 17 years — to an extraordinary performance with musical gloves.

videos.title: Tasha Cobbs Leonard
videos.overview: Tasha Cobbs Leonard is widely regarded as one of the best gospel singers performing today. Her set at the Tiny Desk moved many at the NPR offices to tears.

videos.title: Betty Who
videos.overview: Betty Who brings Roséwave, sun's-out pop to the Tiny Desk with all the usual studio production stripped away.

videos.title: Be More Chill
videos.overview: On Broadway, Be More Chill is a playful burst of frenetic energy and silly, stealthy sweetness. At the Tiny Desk, it holds onto that rowdy, generous spirit while stripping down the arrangements.

videos.title: Saint Sister
videos.overview: The group from Ireland makes music that mixes the organic with the electronic, starting with a large, 34-string lever harp.

videos.title: Miya Folick
videos.overview: Miya Folick was raised a Buddhist in Santa Ana, Calif., and is of Ukrainian and Japanese descent. She sings of conviction, not fiction.

videos.title: American Football
videos.overview: Who would've thought that American Football's fruitful reunion would not only include some of the emo band's best songs, but also a children's choir at the Tiny Desk?

videos.title: Sting And Shaggy
videos.overview: The two musical legends brought plenty of joy to the Tiny Desk, with an unexpected collaboration that works surprisingly well.

videos.title: Erin Rae
videos.overview: Every time she performs live, Erin Rae transforms her quiet storms into different hues of squalling introspection.

videos.title: Priests
videos.overview: The punk-infused art band from Washington, D.C. brings a kinder, gentler and sparer version of the group's music to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Jacob Collier
videos.overview: As the NPR staff gathered to watch his performance, Jacob Collier sprinted full bore down the hallway for his set, hardly able to contain his creative energy or enthusiasm.

videos.title: Masego
videos.overview: The spirit of Cab Calloway lives on in Masego, the singer, producer and multi-instrumentalist who surprised NPR's Tiny Desk audience with a zany sense of showmanship.

videos.title: Tamino
videos.overview: Tamino possesses one of the most remarkable and memorable voices to ever grace the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Lizzo
videos.overview: Backed by a band assembled just for this occasion, the breakthrough pop icon performs three joyfully showy songs from Cuz I Love You.

videos.title: Calexico And Iron & Wine
videos.overview: The two bands just released Years to Burn, their first album together since 2005. Now, they've performed three songs — two new, one old — for Calexico's Tiny Desk debut.

videos.title: iLe
videos.overview: The Calle 13 veteran, fresh off her appearance at demonstrations in Puerto Rico, performs three songs that rage with revolutionary intensity.

videos.title: Bas
videos.overview: Bas came to the Tiny Desk to get it, and — in a breathless four-song set — he did exactly that.

videos.title: David Crosby & The Lighthouse Band
videos.overview: David Crosby, Becca Stevens, Michelle Willis and Michael League are The Lighthouse Band, and together they harmonized the heck out of the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Among Authors
videos.overview: Among Authors' music isn't casual; there are songs within these songs, and they're not always catchy. They'll take you on a journey worth following.

videos.title: half•alive
videos.overview: How does half•alive, known for funky earworms and synchronized dancing, translate to such a cozy space? Have the dancers sit.

videos.title: Kian Soltani
videos.overview: Watch a young cellist on the rise, offering music of virtuosity, sweet lyricism and a little fire from his Persian roots.

videos.title: Tobe Nwigwe
videos.overview: The Houston-based rapper's mindful words are like a life hack for anyone seeking guidance, with pleas to look past inherent hardships and evil and to stay focused on life's ultimate prizes.

videos.title: Nicole Bus
videos.overview: Nicole Bus' sound is reminiscent of vintage R&B, yet still feels current and capable of transcending age and demographics.

videos.title: Mandolin Orange
videos.overview: Andrew Marlin and Emily Frantz made everything seem so easy, with just a few acoustic instruments and a single microphone behind the Tiny Desk, performing songs full of joy and thoughtfulness.

videos.title: 47SOUL
videos.overview: 47SOUL's message of equality is meant for the world. It's music without borders, mixing old and new, acoustic and electronic from a band formed in Amman Jordan, singing in Arabic and English.

videos.title: Dan Tepfer
videos.overview: The pianist and programmer has transformed the acoustic piano into his duet partner.

videos.title: The-Dream
videos.overview: The singer and mega-hit songwriter showcases three of his own tracks, including "I Luv Your Girl" and two songs from Ménage à Trois: Sextape Vol. 1, 2, 3.

videos.title: A-WA
videos.overview: The three Israeli sisters in A-WA mix Yemenite and Arabic traditions with splashes of reggae and hip-hop.

videos.title: The Tallest Man On Earth (2019)
videos.overview: The Tallest Man On Earth's second appearance at the Tiny Desk comes almost 10 years to the day after his first. He returns with a touch of grey and a beard, but no less intense or moving.

videos.title: Damian 'Jr. Gong' Marley
videos.overview: With eyes shut, Marley dug deep into the healing power of music with songs from his 2017 album Stony Hill.

videos.title: Come From Away
videos.overview: Sixteen performers from the Broadway cast crammed behind the Tiny Desk to sing songs and share stories about thousands of airline passengers who were stranded in Newfoundland after 9/11.

videos.title: Rhiannon Giddens
videos.overview: Giddens shares songs from her latest album, There is No Other, in an emotional and transfixing performance at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Nilüfer Yanya
videos.overview: There's a hush to the music of Nilüfer Yanya that made the Tiny Desk the perfect stage for her sound.

videos.title: Y La Bamba
videos.overview: Y La Bamba returns for its second Tiny Desk performance with a revised musical vision.

videos.title: Rosanne Cash
videos.overview: Roseanne Cash has been making great records for forty years, but she's never played or written better music than she's doing right now.

videos.title: Ari Lennox
videos.overview: The R&B singer performed songs from her debut full-length, Shea Butter Baby.

videos.title: Josh Ritter With Amanda Shires And Jason Isbell
videos.overview: In his second visit to the Tiny Desk, Josh Ritter had America on his mind. "We all have to fight against this notion that we're not all human beings."

videos.title: Jonas Brothers
videos.overview: The brothers and their backing band gave a playful performance of three tracks from their latest album, Happiness Begins.

videos.title: Molly Sarlé
videos.overview: After performing at the Tiny Desk as one third of the group Mountain Man, Molly Sarlé returns for a soul-stirring solo performance.

videos.title: Sharon Van Etten
videos.overview: Nearly a decade after her first appearance at the Tiny Desk, Sharon Van Etten returns with a full band and a bigger, bolder sound.

videos.title: Charly Bliss
videos.overview: The vibrancy of the band can feel childlike and candy-coated. But the group's songs are more about the pain of entering adulthood and leaving some of that sweetness behind.

videos.title: Brittany Howard
videos.overview: The Alabama Shakes singer and guitarist brought an eight-piece backing band to the Tiny Desk for a set of deeply personal and affecting songs.

videos.title: Taylor Swift
videos.overview: As she settled in for this stripped-down set, Taylor Swift looked out over the office. "I just decided to take this as an opportunity to show you guys how the songs sounded when I first wrote them."

videos.title: Summer Walker
videos.overview: One week after releasing a record-shattering studio debut, the Atlanta native brings a glowing R&B set to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Jovino Santos Neto Trio
videos.overview: Along with his trio, the pianist, multi-instrumentalist and composer cast a spell over the NPR Music offices in this joyful turn behind the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: CHAI
videos.overview: The group from Japan is on a mission to expand the conventional meaning of "cute." Their performance included synchronized dancing, pom-poms and matching pink uniforms, with a heavy, angular sound.

videos.title: Rio Mira
videos.overview: Rio Mira's music celebrates life along the river that separates Ecuador and Colombia: soft breezes, loving friends, the embrace of Africa and lots of festejando!

videos.title: BJ The Chicago Kid
videos.overview: The 34-year old R&B mainstay used his moment at the desk to fit in as many of his most cherished songs as possible — Nine songs in 17 minutes to be exact.

videos.title: Dave
videos.overview: The British rapper made a trip all the way from the UK just for this Tiny Desk performance and powered through a set that made the personal political.

videos.title: Leslie Odom Jr.
videos.overview: The Tony- and Grammy-winning singer, actor, author and Hamilton star performs three songs from Mr, his genre-bending new solo album.

videos.title: Sunny War
videos.overview: Sunny War has been homeless, busked on city streets and Venice Beach, left home feeling she was a burden to her mother, battled addiction and still found a way to bring joy to others thru her music.

videos.title: KOKOKO!
videos.overview: KOKOKO! are sonic warriors. They seized control of the Tiny Desk, shouting their arrival through a megaphone, while electronic sirens begin to blare.

videos.title: Burna Boy
videos.overview: The Nigerian singer and songwriter is one of the biggest African artists in the world and a pioneer of Afro-fusion, an inescapable sound this year.

videos.title: Snarky Puppy
videos.overview: The jazz, funk and gospel improv group brought jams and joy to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Igor Levit
videos.overview: The insightful pianist offers a Beethoven bonanza, ranging from the mesmerizing pulse of the popular "Moonlight" Sonata to flashes of wry humor and tender beauty.

videos.title: Carly Rae Jepsen
videos.overview: The singer brought a sparkling pop-disco vibe and a lot of swagger to the sun-filled Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Mereba
videos.overview: A nomadic storyteller with a cross-genre style ranging from folk to rap, Mereba slays the devil in her solo set behind the Desk.

videos.title: Black Uhuru
videos.overview: The influential reggae group, whose name means "black freedom," brought songs of solidarity and love to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Freddie Gibbs And Madlib
videos.overview: The enigmatic and reclusive producer Madlib joins hard-hitting emcee Freddie Gibbs for one of the most memorable Tiny Desks of the year.

videos.title: Raveena
videos.overview: "I just want you to know," Raveena told the NPR office, "that in this space that we're in, you're extremely, extremely loved."

videos.title: Weyes Blood
videos.overview: Watch the band perform a blissed-out, gently sweeping set featuring three songs from its latest album, Titanic Rising.

videos.title: The Comet Is Coming
videos.overview: The Comet is Coming is a force of nature. The British trio makes the kind of instrumental jazz that takes music lovers out of their comfort zone and into a musical realm they may never have explored.

videos.title: Moonchild
videos.overview: The LA-based trio makes an intricate blend of jazz, R&B and hip-hop. For their Tiny Desk set, they pulled out all the stops: flutes, flugelhorns, saxophones, keyboards, ukuleles and more.

videos.title: Los Lobos
videos.overview: When Los Lobos gathered behind the Tiny Desk, it felt like they were cramped in the back room of a family Christmas party, calling up tunes from the Latin holiday song book.

videos.title: Balún
videos.overview: It's impossible to not be drawn in by the visual specter of Balún as the band mixes traditional instruments and electronics, set against a rich tapestry of voices.

videos.title: Spanglish Fly
videos.overview: Spanglish Fly is one of the pioneers of the boogaloo revival scene happening on the East Coast. For about sixteen minutes, they turned the NPR Music offices into the hottest Latin dance club in D.C.

videos.title: Daniel Norgren
videos.overview: The Swedish singer sways and writhes as he and his band create a dream state calming enough to slow the day's hectic pace to a crawl. Take a seat on a comfy couch and have a listen.

videos.title: Bridget Kibbey
videos.overview: The irrepressible harpist proves that the instrument can be as tempestuous as a tango, as complex as a Bach fugue and sing as serenely as a church choir.

videos.title: Brownout
videos.overview: The Austin, Texas band brought old-school R&B horns, bongos and deep grooves to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Jordan Rakei
videos.overview: Despite some unexpected gear problems, the soulful R&B artist and his band locked-in and played a phenomenal set behind the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Joyce DiDonato
videos.overview: Watch the celebrated opera star deconstruct old Italian love songs with her signature flair, backed by a crack jazz ensemble.

videos.title: Yola
videos.overview: The singer who once sang for Massive Attack and sampled by Iggy Azalea and The Chemical Brothers, is front-and-center at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Max Richter
videos.overview: The eclectic composer joins members of the ACME ensemble for some of his most affecting music, which moves the audience to tears.

videos.title: J.S. Ondara
videos.overview: After first trying to win our annual Tiny Desk Contest, the singer-songwriter from Nairobi decided to put out a record, got nominated for a Grammy and wound up here anyway

videos.title: Koffee
videos.overview: The fast-rising teenager from Jamaica just won a Grammy for Best Reggae Album, making her the first woman and youngest artist to ever win in the category.

videos.title: Jimmy Eat World
videos.overview: Jimmy Eat World showed up to the NPR Music office all smiles and no guitars. They borrowed a couple acoustics, a gong and a tambourine for a heartfelt set that included "The Middle."

videos.title: Rising Appalachia
videos.overview: The Atlanta-based band came to NPR in a van packed with a bodhrán (Irish drum), an ngoni (West African harp) a huge gourd, a cello, a baritone guitar and more.

videos.title: SiR
videos.overview: The R&B singer from Inglewood, CA made his performance a family affair, dedicating it to his late godson, with his mother and older brother on backup vocals.

videos.title: Another Sky
videos.overview: The strength of this London band is matching message with music. There's intensity and clear intention in their use of rock as an art.

videos.title: Jonathan Scales Fourchestra
videos.overview: Here's a first: Steelpans at the Tiny Desk. It's true. Nearly a thousand performances into the series and the instrument has never been featured, until now.

videos.title: Baby Rose
videos.overview: At 25, she mixes the bluesy melisma of Nina Simone and the deep register of Sarah Vaughan — two of her influences — with songwriting as devastating as her delivery.

videos.title: Mount Eerie with Julie Doiron
videos.overview: Phil Elverum shares his open wounds — of death, love and the loss of love — in close harmonies, accompanied only by electric and nylon-string guitars.

videos.title: Laura Stevenson
videos.overview: Backed by a small string section, Stevenson performed three songs that sounded so gorgeous, an actual marriage proposal broke out shortly after her set ended.

videos.title: Snoh Aalegra
videos.overview: The Iranian-Swedish singer draws her musical cues from Brandy and Sade while racking up a list of collaborators such as Vince Staples, James Fauntleroy and, most recently, Pharrell Williams.

videos.title: Elisapie
videos.overview: The Canadian singer-songwriter gives a deep, soulful performance against a sometimes moody backdrop of bass saxophone and bowed guitars.

videos.title: Chris Dave and the Drumhedz
videos.overview: Chris Dave, your favorite musician's favorite drummer, takes listeners on a journey through a virtual record store, picking up different genres along the way and putting them in your bag.

videos.title: Jenny Lewis
videos.overview: A consummate storyteller, going as far back to her days with her band Rilo Kiley, the words of Jenny Lewis comfort and inspire.

videos.title: Indigo Sparke
videos.overview: The Australian singer transforms the NPR Music offices with a voice that, at moments, comes as a whisper.

videos.title: Cimafunk
videos.overview: The band from Havana brings its intoxicating mix of Afro-Cuban dance music and 1970s funk-and-soul to the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: Bob Weir and Wolf Bros
videos.overview: Weir, along with Don Was and Jay Lane, play a set rich in Grateful Dead lore, including an emotional take on the sing-along, "Ripple."

videos.title: Mellotron Variations
videos.overview: Robby Grant, Pat Sansone (Wilco), Jonathan Kirkscey and John Medeski (Medeski, Martin & Wood) give an all-Mellotron performance, making music of magic and mystery.

videos.title: Terri Lyne Carrington + Social Science
videos.overview: The veteran jazz drummer is joined by special guests that include producer and percussionist Kassa Overall and actor Malcolm Jamal Warner, for a potent and deeply moving set.

videos.title: Taimane

videos.title: Coldplay

videos.title: Kirill Gerstein
videos.overview: Watch the award-winning pianist play a hit by Chopin, a premiere by Thomas Adès and a cherished song by Gershwin dressed in a virtuosic arrangement.

videos.title: Chika

videos.title: Harry Styles
videos.overview: The former One Direction singer gave a charming performance of "Watermelon Sugar," "Adore You" and other cuts from his latest album, Fine Line.

videos.title: Rex Orange County
videos.overview: Watch the low-key British pop star perform "Sunflower," "Loving Is Easy" and more at the Tiny Desk.

videos.title: The Baylor Project

videos.title: Dua Lipa

videos.title: ARTEMIS
videos.overview:
Yes, ARTEMIS is named for a Greek goddess. This jazz supergroup has super powers and they're on full display from beginning to end during this Tiny Desk. The multi-generational and multinational group is composed of pianist Renee Rosnes, drummer (and Tiny Desk alum) Allison Miller, bassist Noriko Ueda, trumpeter Ingrid Jensen and tenor saxophonist Nicole Glover, all bandleaders with their own prolific outputs.
